title: AI is shifting the value of work toward judgment, oversight, hybrid capability and broad AI literacy rather than eliminating the need for human agency
source_unit: European Training Foundation, Changing Landscape of Skills in the Age of AI, prepared through the Inter-Agency TVET Working Group with Cedefop, Eurofound, European Commission, ILO and UNESCO
geography: Cross-sector and international synthesis of AI-related changes in workplace skills and skills policy

observations.period: 2026 report; workplace task and skill re-composition

cognitive_demand.value: AI adoption is associated with greater demand for higher-order analytical ability, critical thinking, problem solving, contextualization and judgment

human_ai_collaboration.value: work shifts from pure creation toward framing, editorial review, appraisal and oversight of AI outputs

hybrid_roles.value: traditional occupational expertise is increasingly combined with digital, computational and data literacy

observations.method: Inter-agency literature and analytical synthesis linking AI use to tasks, cognitive skills, socio-emotional skills and manual-skill complementarities across occupations.
observations.uncertainty: The report synthesizes evidence from different studies and does not estimate one universal causal effect of AI adoption on skill demand; effects vary by task, sector, technology design and worker capability.
observations.subgroup: Workers, managers, educators, professional users, technical specialists and people in occupations with routine or non-routine cognitive, socio-emotional and manual tasks.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some AI deployments may deskill work, intensify monitoring or reduce autonomy even when aggregate demand for higher-order skills rises; skill complementarity is not guaranteed for every worker.

denominator.unit: global employment frame used in reviewed studies

ai_workforce_range.unit: percent of total employment, depending on definitions and analytical method, involved in developing or professionally using AI

technical_workforce_growth.value: demand for AI-related technical skills has increased rapidly over the past decade

concentration.value: AI work is concentrated in highly educated, prime-age professionals, with developers especially concentrated among white men

observations.method: Comparative review of definitions, estimates and occupational profiles for the emerging AI workforce.
observations.uncertainty: The wide 0.3–5 percent range reflects different definitions of AI workforce, exposure and professional use; workforce composition varies by country and occupation.
observations.subgroup: AI developers and engineers, professional users, ICT and scientific workers, workers seeking entry into AI-enabled roles, and groups with unequal access to advanced education.
observations.counterinterpretation: A small direct AI workforce can still produce broad indirect effects through tools embedded in ordinary jobs; concentration today does not establish permanent exclusion from future AI-related work.

observations.period: 2026 report; AI literacy as a foundational capability

ai_literacy.value: ability to understand and use AI tools safely and ethically
ai_literacy.unit: foundational capability identified by the report

technical_literacy.value: basic understanding of how AI systems, machine learning, algorithms and data-driven technologies work

analytical_data_literacy.value: capacity to interpret and assess AI outputs in real-world situations

ethical_societal_literacy.value: awareness of privacy, bias, transparency, accountability, fairness and sustainability

observations.method: Policy framework synthesis across education, training, work, government services, media, finance, healthcare and education contexts.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies a capability direction and policy need; it does not establish a common validated measure of AI literacy or prove that training produces equal agency across populations.
observations.subgroup: Workers, students, teachers, trainers, adult learners, service users and citizens affected by AI-mediated institutions and information environments.
observations.counterinterpretation: Literacy alone cannot correct opaque systems, unequal compute access, coercive workplace deployment, weak privacy protections or absent redress; institutional safeguards remain necessary.

observations.period: 2026 report; education, training and labour-market policy response

capability_shift.value: skills policy should prioritize broader capabilities, agility, resilience, adaptability and human agency rather than narrow task-specific skills

learning_pathways.value: AI learning needs to run across initial education, higher education, adult learning, workplace training and teacher or trainer development

assessment_need.value: curriculum, certification, assessment and quality-assurance systems need reform as AI changes task boundaries

observations.method: Inter-agency synthesis of curriculum, qualification, teacher, adult-learning, workplace-upskilling and assessment implications.
observations.uncertainty: The report provides policy implications rather than an implementation evaluation; country capacity, employer incentives, access, language and affordability will shape results.
observations.subgroup: Education and training systems, teachers, trainers, employers, workers, jobseekers, students and public agencies responsible for skills and labour-market transitions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Broad capability frameworks can become vague or burdensome without clear occupational pathways, recognized credentials, protected learning time and employer or public investment.

ILO labour-market context on job quality, informality, inequality and AI risk.

boundary: This record adds an AI-to-capability route: workplace AI changes the value of judgment, oversight, hybrid expertise, socio-emotional skill and broad AI literacy, while technical AI work remains concentrated. It is an inter-agency synthesis and policy framework, not worker-level task data, an adoption measurement, a causal employment evaluation or a guarantee that AI produces more autonomy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official ILO publication page and linked 60-page PDF were retrieved and reviewed for task and skill recomposition, AI workforce range and composition, AI literacy domains, human agency and education and training implications; the PDF was hashed.
